q: You have Microsoft Defender XDR. The server team must receive an email when a device from the Servers device group is isolated, either manually or automatically, and when isolation fails. What should you configure?
options: A notification rule in the Incidents tab with severity High.
An alert tuning rule with the Resolve alert action.
A notification rule in the Actions tab with Action source manual and automated, device group scope Servers and statuses completed and failed.
An automation rule in Sentinel with the Add tags action.
explain: The Actions tab in Email notifications sends notifications about response actions, with a choice of source (manual/automated), actions, device groups and statuses. The Incidents tab is for incidents, and alert tuning and automation rules do not send email.

q: Which permission is required to configure email notifications in Microsoft Defender XDR when using Defender RBAC?
options: Manage security settings
Security Reader
Live response (advanced)
Microsoft Sentinel Responder
explain: Email notifications require Manage security settings (in the basic model, Security Administrator or higher). With RBAC, a user manages only notifications for the device groups they have access to.

q: An internal backup tool triggers the same Defender for Endpoint alert every night. The alert must not create an incident, but the events must remain available in AlertInfo and AlertEvidence for hunting. What should you do?
options: Add the tool's file as an Allow indicator.
Create an alert tuning rule with the Hide alert action and a condition on the tool's process.
Turn off the advanced feature Automatically resolve alerts.
Create a custom detection rule that excludes the tool.
explain: Hide alert (MDE alerts only) suppresses the alert and prevents an incident, while the alert remains in AlertInfo and AlertEvidence. An Allow indicator changes protection behavior, and a custom detection does not affect built-in alerts.

q: An alert tuning rule does not suppress alerts generated by your custom detection rule. What is the cause?
options: The rule has more than 200 conditions.
The Resolve alert action works only for Defender for Office 365.
The custom detection must have a Continuous (NRT) frequency.
Alert tuning does not apply to alerts from custom detection rules; the noise must be handled in the query.
explain: The documentation states that alert tuning is not compatible with custom detections; they should be fine-tuned in the query itself.

q: An organization has regional SOC teams that see only the device groups of their region. They need to be able to take over incidents without alerts from other regions being merged into the same incident. What should you turn on?
options: The advanced feature Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups.
Alert tuning with the Set as behavior action.
Automation level No automated response for all groups.
Email notifications per device group.
explain: Restrict correlation to within scoped device groups prevents alerts from different device groups from being merged into one incident, so the local SOC can work on its own incident. The global SOC then sees more, smaller incidents.

q: Analysts can start live response on workstations, but not on Windows Server devices. What should you turn on?
options: Tamper protection
Live response unsigned script execution
Live response for servers
EDR in block mode
explain: Live response for servers is a separate advanced feature. Unsigned script execution allows unsigned scripts, but does not enable live response on servers.

q: You want to block execution of a specific file by SHA-256 hash on all devices through Indicators in Defender for Endpoint. The option is not available. What should you check?
options: That Device discovery is turned on.
That the advanced feature Allow or block file is turned on, with Defender Antivirus as the active AV and cloud-based protection.
That Custom network indicators is turned on.
That the device group has automation level Full.
explain: Blocking files requires the advanced feature Allow or block file, and the prerequisites are Defender Antivirus as the active AV and cloud-based protection. Custom network indicators is for IP, domain and URL.

q: You created a custom data collection rule for the DeviceCustomScriptEvents table scoped to the manually added tag Finance-Servers. After two hours there is not a single event. What is the MOST LIKELY cause?
options: The rule takes up to 24 hours to deploy.
Custom data collection works only on Linux.
DeviceCustomScriptEvents is not a supported table.
Custom data collection supports only dynamic tags from Asset Rule Management.
explain: Manual (static) tags are not supported; you need a dynamic tag rule in Asset Rule Management that has run at least once. Deployment takes 20 minutes to 1 hour, and Windows 10/11 and Server 2019+ are supported.

q: Where is data from Defender for Endpoint custom data collection rules written?
options: To the connected Microsoft Sentinel workspace, in DeviceCustom* tables.
Only to Defender XDR advanced hunting, for 30 days.
To an Azure Storage account defined in the rule.
To the DeviceEvents table with ActionType Custom.
explain: Custom data collection sends additional events to the connected Sentinel workspace (DeviceCustomProcessEvents, DeviceCustomFileEvents, DeviceCustomNetworkEvents, DeviceCustomScriptEvents, DeviceCustomImageLoadEvents), and that ingestion is billed at Sentinel prices.

q: You need to introduce the ASR rule Block all Office applications from creating child processes without disrupting business macros. What should you do FIRST?
options: Set the rule to Block and wait for user reports.
Set the rule to Audit and analyze DeviceEvents where ActionType starts with Asr.
Add all Office folders to ASR exclusions.
Set the rule to Warn on all devices.
explain: Audit records what would have been blocked without affecting users. After the analysis, targeted exclusions are added and the rule is switched to Block. Excluding all Office folders defeats the protection.

q: A remediation action on a file in C:\Windows\System32 is awaiting approval, while the same action on a file in the Downloads folder was executed automatically. Which automation level does the device group have?
options: Full - remediate threats automatically
Semi - require approval for all folders
Semi - require approval for core folders remediation
No automated response
explain: The core folders level requires approval only for system folders (e.g. \windows\*), and everything else runs automatically. All folders would also require approval for Downloads.

q: Production servers must require approval for every remediation action, while workstations should remain fully automated. What should you do?
options: Change the automation level of the Ungrouped devices (default) group to Semi - require approval for all folders.
Turn off automatic attack disruption for the whole tenant.
Add the servers to alert tuning with the Resolve alert action.
Create a device group for the servers with Semi - require approval for all folders and a rank above the workstation group.
explain: The automation level is set per device group. A device belongs to the highest-ranked group whose rules it matches, so the server group needs a higher rank. Changing the default group would also affect workstations.

q: According to the change that took effect on 1 September 2026, what happened to automated investigation and response (AIR) in Defender for Endpoint?
options: AIR no longer works as a separate investigation experience and cannot be started manually; its capabilities are part of the default AV protection, and a full antivirus scan is recommended for on-demand investigation.
AIR was moved to Microsoft Sentinel playbooks.
AIR was also discontinued for Defender for Office 365.
AIR is now started only from custom detection rules.
explain: From 1 Sep 2026, AIR in MDE is neither separate nor manually startable; it works automatically through AV protection. Integrations that manually started AIR need to be adjusted. AIR for Defender for Office 365 remains.

q: Automatic attack disruption must never disable the emergency-admin account, while everything else should remain automatic. What should you configure?
options: Set all device groups to No automated response.
Open an Attack disruption opt-out support request.
Add a user exclusion in Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Automated response > Identities.
Add the account to IP exclusions.
explain: A user exclusion prevents automatic disabling of only that account. Opt-out and No automated response would turn off protection more broadly than needed, and IP exclusions apply to addresses, not accounts.

q: In Sentinel, an automation rule cannot select a playbook because the playbook is grayed out in the list. What should you do?
options: Assign the analyst the Logic App Contributor role.
Change the playbook trigger to Microsoft Sentinel entity.
Assign the analyst the Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator role.
Through Manage playbook permissions, assign the Sentinel service account the Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor role on the playbook's resource group.
explain: Automation rules run playbooks through the Sentinel service account, which needs Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group. For that assignment, the user needs Owner on that resource group.

q: You have two automation rules with the When incident is created trigger: Rule A (order 1) changes severity from Medium to Low, Rule B (order 2) adds a tag only for incidents with severity Medium or higher. A severity Medium incident is created to which both rules apply. What happens?
options: Both rules run in parallel, so the tag is added.
Rule B does not add the tag, because it sees the incident after Rule A changed it to Low.
Rule B runs first because it has a higher number.
Rule B adds the tag, because conditions are always evaluated against the original state.
explain: Automation rules run sequentially by order number, and a later rule evaluates the current state of the incident after the previous rules.

q: During a penetration test from 3 to 7 November, incidents from IP address 10.10.5.20 should be automatically closed as benign positive, and after the test the rule must no longer run. Which TWO automation rule settings should you use? (Choose TWO.)
options: The action Change status → Closed with the reason Benign Positive.
The action Run playbook with a Logic App that closes the incident.
Expiration date 7 November.
Trigger When alert is created.
Condition Incident provider equals Microsoft Sentinel.
explain: Closing with a reason is a built-in automation rule action, and the expiration date automatically turns off the rule. A playbook is not needed, and the Incident provider condition has been removed in the Defender portal.

q: Order the steps for an automation rule to run a new playbook that opens a ServiceNow ticket for every new incident, from first to last.
options: Create an automation rule with the When incident is created trigger and the Run playbook action.
Create a Logic App playbook with the Microsoft Sentinel incident trigger and a ServiceNow connection.
Create a test incident and verify that the ticket was opened.
Through Manage playbook permissions, grant Sentinel Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor on the playbook's resource group.
explain: First the playbook with the incident trigger is created, then Sentinel gets permission to run it, then the automation rule attaches the playbook to new incidents, and finally the flow is tested.

q: Match each requirement with the tool that BEST fulfills it.
options: Automatically assign all incidents from the Brute force rule to analyst Ana.
Enrich an incident with WHOIS data from an external API.
Prevent a Defender for Endpoint alert for a known admin tool from creating an incident.
During an active ransomware attack, automatically contain the compromised account.
Receive an email when a new threat analytics report is published.
explain: Assigning an owner is a built-in automation rule action, calling an external API requires a playbook, suppressing a known alert is done by alert tuning, containment during an attack is done by attack disruption, and notifications about reports by the Threat analytics tab.

q: Match each Sentinel role with its purpose.
options: Microsoft Sentinel Automation Contributor
Microsoft Sentinel Playbook Operator
Microsoft Sentinel Responder
Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
targets: Attaching a playbook to an analytics or automation rule
Allows automation rules (the Sentinel service account) to run playbooks
Access to the incident for a manual run, without running the playbook itself
explain: Automation Contributor is for the service account and automation rules, Playbook Operator for manual runs, Responder for working with incidents (but it does not run playbooks), and Contributor for attaching playbooks to rules.
